tasks.title: Implement explicit Job, Phase, Attempt, and control transition guards
tasks.rationale: Current mutable status fields do not define legal transitions, attempts, fencing, immutable terminal truth, or stale-result behavior.
tasks.evidence: REQ-014–REQ-017; GAP-007, GAP-008; state reconstruction in Sections 3 and 10.
tasks.files: Create `atlas/models/states.py`, `atlas/core/lifecycle.py`; refactor `atlas/core/orchestrator.py`; add migrations/tables for phase runs and attempts.
requirements: Define exhaustive legal transition tables and guards for jobs, phase runs, attempts, and control requests.
Represent each execution as a new immutable attempt with attempt number, backend identity, lease/fencing token, start/end, outcome, error class, checkpoint reference, and result digest.
Make terminal job/phase/attempt states immutable except through explicit reconciliation records.
Define failure propagation, skip reasons, suspension, cancellation, retry scheduling, restart, and replay semantics.
Reject late results whose fencing token or expected state no longer matches.
invariants: Illegal transitions cannot be persisted.
A terminal record cannot silently become non-terminal.
Only the coordinator transaction can advance lifecycle authority.
A stale attempt can never overwrite a newer attempt.
edges: Duplicate completion; cancel during retry delay; pause at terminal phase; resume non-suspended job; late worker result; crash after external effect but before result commit.
tasks.failure: Guard rejection is deterministic and leaves state unchanged; unknown side-effect outcome enters `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, not automatic retry.
tasks.security: Fencing tokens are unguessable or monotonic within authoritative state; control actor/adapter identity is recorded; no API/CLI bypass.
tasks.observability: Transition counters by from/to/result, rejection reason, attempt age, stale-result count, terminal-state audit record.
tasks.tests: Exhaustive table/property tests, concurrent transition races, stale fencing, duplicate command idempotency, crash-point integration.
accept: Every transition documented in Section 10 has a direct positive and negative test.
Concurrent incompatible transitions yield one committed winner and deterministic loser errors.
Terminal-state immutability and stale-result rejection are proven under concurrency.
Legacy status strings project consistently for compatibility readers.
tasks.migration: Map legacy `completed→SUCCEEDED`, `error→FAILED`; create attempt 1 for active/historical phase rows where provenance is sufficient, otherwise mark `legacy_unattributed`.
tasks.rollback: Compatibility projection permits old readers; rollback restores pre-migration DB, not ad-hoc state rewrites.
tasks.completion: Machine-readable transition table, exhaustive test report, migration mapping, and concurrency/fencing evidence.

Downstream phases receive only `intake_generation_id` and occurrence IDs.

Accepted manifests are immutable observation records.
A path is an occurrence locator, not content identity.

tasks.title: Persist occurrence-to-content identity using canonical SHA-256
tasks.rationale: Current hashes are process-local and disconnected from accepted occurrences, preventing cross-run deduplication and exact-byte lineage.
tasks.files: Create/extend `atlas/artifacts/models.py`, `atlas/artifacts/hasher.py`; refactor `atlas/storage/hash_store.py`, `atlas/phases/fingerprinting.py`; migrations.
requirements: Canonical identity is `sha256:<hex>`; optional BLAKE3 is acceleration/integrity metadata, never the sole canonical identity.

Fingerprint only accepted regular-file occurrences; open through canonical source access (AT-009 integration point), stream bytes, validate pre/post handle metadata, and persist occurrence↔content relation atomically.
Recognize one content identity across many occurrences and runs.
Record hash algorithm/version, byte count, read start/end, mutation result, and capture/storage status.
Keep hashing separate from blob retention; CAS arrives in AT-011.
invariants: Path, size, name, and timestamp never equal byte identity.
One SHA-256 identity may bind many occurrences; an occurrence generation binds at most one verified content identity.
Mutated/stale reads never receive a false binding.
edges: File truncates/appends/replaces during read; sparse/large file; duplicate bytes; interrupted hash; unsupported special file; BLAKE3 unavailable.
tasks.failure: Mutation yields a typed stale-source result and blocks dependent work according policy; interrupted hashes create no content binding.
tasks.security: Race-resistant source opening, bounded read buffers, no active-content execution, digest comparison in constant behavior where applicable.
tasks.observability: Bytes hashed, throughput, duplicate hit/miss, mutation failures, algorithm/version, restart dedup result.
tasks.tests: Source swap/truncate/append, duplicate bytes in multiple paths/runs, multi-gigabyte streaming fixture/procedure, restart dedup, algorithm compatibility.
accept: Cross-process/restart reprocessing recognizes existing SHA-256 identities.
Source mutation cannot attach the wrong identity to an occurrence.
No phase independently invents content IDs.
Legacy `HashStore.has_content()` compatibility behavior is covered.
tasks.migration: Import verified legacy SHA-256 values as orphan `ContentIdentity` rows only; do not fabricate occurrence bindings.
tasks.rollback: Compatibility facade can read new identities; additive tables permit reverting code after DB backup.
tasks.completion: Identity schema, hash service, restart/mutation test artifacts, duplicate metrics, and migration report.

Coalesce/sample high-volume progress events while keeping current progress authoritative.
Preserve legacy routing keys through a versioned adapter.
invariants: A successful required transition always has its durable event.
Transport success/failure never defines lifecycle state.
Event ordering is deterministic per authoritative store.
Redelivery cannot duplicate an authoritative effect.

accept: Every required state transition query returns its durable event in the same committed transaction.

tasks.title: Introduce quarantine workspaces and recursive cumulative archive budgets

requirements: Create unique per-job/phase/attempt quarantine workspaces outside source roots with quotas and restrictive permissions.

Inspect nested containers recursively through a bounded work queue before materialization where feasible; enforce cumulative depth, member count, declared/actual expanded bytes, per-file bytes, compression ratio, temp bytes, and wall time.
Canonicalize member names and reject absolute, parent traversal, NUL, reserved/device, symlink/hardlink/device entries unless an explicit safe policy exists.

No materialization precedes an accepted report for exact bytes.
Budgets are cumulative across nested containers and actual writes.
Every materialized regular file receives content identity and lineage.

tasks.security: Required core control; active content is never executed; secure temp/open flags; no source-adjacent writes; total-job budgets.
tasks.observability: Nested depth, member/byte budgets, actual versus declared bytes, quarantine usage, rejection reasons, cleanup status.
tasks.tests: Adversarial archive corpus, generated path/member properties, nested bombs, disk-full fault injection, partial extraction cleanup, no-write-under-source assertion.
accept: All adversarial archives terminate within configured resource bounds.

tasks.title: Define versioned typed plugin descriptors and a deterministic registry

edges: Duplicate ID; incompatible API version; malformed result; unavailable external tool; nondeterministic plugin marked cacheable; 0/50/51/large findings; plugin crash.

tasks.security: Capability least privilege; no direct StateStore; no implicit source/network; secret references mediated; output schema and size limits.
tasks.observability: Registry snapshot/digest, plugin load/disable reason, execution/resource metrics, finding counts, cache eligibility/hit/miss.
tasks.tests: Registry determinism, version compatibility, duplicate conflict, malformed/oversized results, attribution, losslessness, AI authority negative tests.
accept: No arbitrary dictionary reaches durable findings.
Two clean registry builds produce the same ordered snapshot/digest.
More than 50 findings persist losslessly within declared limits.
A plugin cannot invoke lifecycle transitions through its context.
tasks.migration: Wrap legacy `AnalyzerPlugin` behind an adapter with generated descriptor and deprecation warning; mark provenance as legacy where fields are unknown.
tasks.rollback: Disable new plugin discovery and retain adapter for legacy trusted plugins; findings remain readable.
tasks.completion: Plugin API/schema, registry snapshot artifact, compatibility tests, normalized finding fixtures, and security contract.

tasks.title: Separate lifecycle semantics from execution location with ExecutionBackend
tasks.rationale: A stable work/result contract is required before isolation or remote execution; the backend must never own lifecycle state.
tasks.files: Create `atlas/execution/base.py`, `atlas/execution/inprocess.py`; integrate coordinator/plugins; later `subprocess.py` in AT-020.
requirements: Define `WorkSpec` containing immutable operation, plugin/version, input identity references, config/policy digests, resource limits, deadline, idempotency key, and fencing token.
Define `WorkResult` with status, output references/digest, diagnostics, resource usage, and echoed authority fields.
Implement trusted in-process backend first and backend conformance suite.
Coordinator alone validates result and transitions attempts/phases; backend cannot access StateStore authority.
Support cancellation/deadline protocol and stale-result rejection.
invariants: Execution location does not change lifecycle semantics.
Backend result cannot advance state without coordinator validation.
Exact work key defines duplicate/replay behavior.
All backends pass the same conformance contract.
edges: Timeout; backend loss; duplicate result; stale fencing; malformed/oversized output; cancellation race; backend shutdown.
tasks.failure: Unknown result or lost backend leaves attempt timed out/lost/reconciliation-required according operation contract; no blind success.
tasks.security: Minimize backend credentials/context; mediated artifact access; signed/authenticated protocol deferred to remote adapter but fields reserved.
tasks.observability: Queue/run latency, backend health, resource usage, cancellations, stale/malformed results, conformance version.
tasks.tests: In-process conformance, identical analyzer through direct/contract path, cancellation/timeout/stale results, serialization compatibility.
accept: A bundled analyzer produces identical normalized findings through the backend contract.
Backend code has no direct lifecycle write capability.
Stale/malformed/duplicate results are rejected deterministically.
Conformance suite is reusable for AT-020/022.
tasks.migration: Route trusted built-ins through in-process backend behind existing APIs; preserve direct plugin adapter during transition.
tasks.rollback: Switch coordinator to compatibility direct executor while retaining WorkSpec/Result records for new jobs only.
tasks.completion: Contracts, in-process backend, conformance suite, equivalence evidence, and authority-boundary documentation.

tasks.title: Implement first-class findings, evidence, decisions, and publication attempts
tasks.rationale: Review currently produces transient candidates rather than durable approve/reject/hold decisions and verifiable publications.
tasks.evidence: GAP-011, GAP-015, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-027, REQ-028; [ATLAS:efa547cafc64b58d60d19dcc1e5ba32c6b046bc5:atlas/phases/review.py:L19-L236].
tasks.files: Create `atlas/review/service.py`, `atlas/review/publication.py`; refactor `atlas/phases/review.py`; extend artifact/finding models and migrations.
requirements: Persist normalized findings separately from evidence records, promotion decisions, publication requests/attempts, and destination verification.
Define decision states `APPROVE/REJECT/HOLD` with actor/policy identity, exact evidence-set digest, reason, time, and supersession rules.
Require an authorized current decision before publication; harmless local jobs may use explicit policy decisions without interactive approval.
Use staged destination writes, idempotency keys, verification, no-replace/expected-replace semantics, and unknown-outcome reconciliation.
Provide bidirectional lineage from publication to exact source bytes and from source occurrence to all derived publications.
invariants: Finding ≠ evidence ≠ decision ≠ publication.
AI/plugin assertions cannot self-promote to trusted evidence/decision.
A decision is bound to an exact evidence set and policy version.
Unknown external outcome is never blindly retried.
edges: Hold/reject; evidence superseded; destination already exists; partial external write; timeout after destination commit; duplicate request; destination outage.
tasks.failure: Publication failure/unknown remains a non-success attempt with reconciliation instructions; no promotion record implies destination success.
tasks.security: Destination policy/capability restrictions, optional deployment authorization, secret references, path/command injection prevention, immutable attribution.
tasks.observability: Decision latency/outcomes, stale evidence, publication attempts/reconciliation, destination verification, lineage query diagnostics.
tasks.tests: Approve/reject/hold E2E, stale evidence negative, duplicate/partial/unknown publication, unauthorized adapter, bidirectional lineage.
accept: Every publication traces to exact source and derived content identities, findings, evidence, decision, policy, actor, and attempt.
Reject/hold cannot publish.
Unknown destination outcome enters reconciliation and does not auto-repeat mutation.
AI/plugin-only output cannot create an approved decision.
tasks.migration: Legacy promotion candidates remain historical summaries with `decision_authority=none`; they are never treated as approved publications.
tasks.rollback: Disable publication adapters; retain decisions/evidence as read-only records; restore DB for schema rollback.
tasks.completion: Review/publication schemas, adapter contract, E2E/fault evidence, lineage export, and operator status.

tasks.title: Define retries, timeouts, idempotency, reconciliation, and crash recovery per phase
tasks.rationale: Replay is unsafe unless each operation declares duplicate effects, checkpoints, and unknown-outcome handling.
tasks.files: Coordinator/lifecycle, phase contracts, execution backends, review/publication; create error/recovery policy module if needed.
requirements: Define typed error taxonomy and per-operation retryability, maximum attempts, backoff/jitter, deadline, idempotency key, checkpoint/restart mode, and reconciliation hook.
Classify built-in operations as pure/restartable, checkpoint-resumable, idempotent side effect, or externally reconcilable side effect.
On startup, scan nonterminal attempts and deterministically resume, retry, reconcile, block, or fail based on verified state.
Never automatically retry an operation with unknown duplicate effects.
Retain failed attempt evidence and link successor attempts.
invariants: Anything that may run twice has declared duplicate-effect behavior.
Recovery resumes from verified durable state, not memory.
Unknown outcome cannot become success or blind retry.
Retries create new attempts and retain predecessors.
edges: Crash before/after every transaction and external write; timeout while child still runs; stale checkpoint; repeated host restarts; dependency outage; retry storm.
tasks.failure: Unreconcilable/unsafe state becomes `BLOCKED/RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` with operator evidence; retry budget exhaustion is terminal under policy.
tasks.security: Bound retries/resources, no secret leakage in errors, external reconciliation uses least privilege and exact idempotency identity.
tasks.observability: Attempt/retry/recovery counters, reason codes, backoff, checkpoint age, unresolved outcomes, restart recovery summary.
tasks.tests: Subprocess kill/fault injection at durable points for every built-in phase, repeated restart, retry exhaustion, external unknown outcome, stale checkpoint.
accept: Every built-in phase has a documented/tested operation-semantics classification.
Crash matrix yields one deterministic recovery decision per fault point.
No side-effecting unknown outcome is automatically repeated.
Recovery diagnostics identify exact attempt/checkpoint/effect boundary.
tasks.migration: Legacy active jobs are classified conservatively as nonresumable unless exact durable evidence proves safe continuation.
tasks.rollback: Disable automatic recovery and require manual block/restart for new jobs; never weaken unknown-outcome safeguards.
tasks.completion: Recovery matrix implementation, phase semantics registry, crash-test artifacts, and startup recovery report.

tasks.title: Add a long-running local daemon as the authoritative active-job owner
tasks.rationale: A CLI process cannot durably own jobs or honor controls from another process; hydrating private `_jobs` is not control.
tasks.evidence: GAP-007, REQ-014, REQ-015; README remaining limitation on process-local controls.
tasks.files: Create `atlas/service/daemon.py`; refactor `atlas/cli.py`, runtime/coordinator; add claim/lease tables as needed.
requirements: Run a single local owner/claim loop that discovers runnable jobs, claims with lease/fencing token, executes/recoveries, and renews authority.
CLI submits commands and reads status through shared command/state service; it never edits private runtime maps.
Support graceful shutdown, abandoned-claim recovery, single-instance lock or multi-owner-safe claims, and health/readiness.
Keep same-process library mode for tests/embedded use under explicit ownership contract.
Do not add remote/distributed workers.
tasks.interfaces: `AtlasDaemon`, `JobClaim`, `CommandService`, local IPC choice or database-mediated commands; unchanged public CLI verbs.
invariants: Exactly one valid fenced owner advances an attempt.
CLI never manufactures active runtime state.
Daemon restart preserves durable lifecycle semantics.
Embedded and daemon modes use the same coordinator rules.
edges: Two daemons; stale lease; host sleep; daemon kill; CLI during shutdown; database lock; orphan subprocess.
tasks.failure: Lost lease stops authority; stale owner result rejected; readiness false on unusable store; claims recover after expiry/reconciliation.
tasks.security: Local IPC/database permissions, actor attribution, no unauthenticated network listener by default, least-privileged daemon account.
tasks.observability: Daemon identity/uptime, claim/lease age, runnable queue, recovery actions, health/readiness, shutdown status.
tasks.tests: Launch daemon and second CLI process pause/resume/cancel; competing-daemon claim test; kill/restart; stale fencing; embedded equivalence.
accept: Separate CLI process controls a job executing under daemon ownership.
Private `_jobs` hydration/mutation is removed from CLI.
Competing daemon cannot double-execute a fenced attempt.
Graceful and forced restart produce deterministic recovery.
tasks.migration: CLI defaults may remain foreground for one window; add explicit `atlas daemon`/connection detection and deprecation path.
tasks.rollback: Return to foreground mode for new jobs only; existing daemon-owned nonterminal jobs are blocked/recovered safely, not stolen.
tasks.completion: Daemon/service code plan, ownership tests, health/status output, operator runbook, and compatibility behavior.

tasks.title: Provide canonical status, telemetry, health, and diagnostic bundles

Expose canonical job status projection: current phase/attempt, progress, pending control, checkpoint, blocker, retry, resource budget, outbox backlog, provenance completeness.
Define metrics and optional traces without making them authoritative.

Redact secrets and bound payload-derived text/path samples.

Logs/metrics/traces never replace durable evidence.

Health/readiness semantics are deterministic and tested.

tasks.title: Implement REST, RabbitMQ, and webhook adapters over the shared command/event contracts
tasks.rationale: External interfaces are useful only after durable semantics exist and must not create alternate lifecycle authority.

tasks.rollback: Remove/disable adapters without changing core state or job executability.

tasks.title: Add subprocess execution with mediated artifacts and enforceable limits
tasks.rationale: Third-party analyzers should not share process authority, unrestricted filesystem, or StateStore credentials.
tasks.files: Create `atlas/execution/subprocess.py`; extend plugin descriptors/policy and workspace/artifact access.

Enforce timeout/termination, output size, temp storage, process count, and platform-available CPU/memory constraints; report unsupported controls.
Network and external tool access are denied by default and explicitly declared/policy-granted.
Sanitize environment, working directory, inherited descriptors, PATH/tool resolution, and secrets.
Treat containers/sandboxes as later backend adapters, not mandatory core.

tasks.title: Add PostgreSQL and object-storage adapters only after measured trigger conditions

tasks.title: Establish continuous release-quality gates and benchmark evidence
tasks.deps: Begins with AT-001 and expands as each task lands
